30 Days of Finding Clues About Jesus in the Heroes

A Note for Parents


Have you ever played a game of detective? You put on a hat. You grab a magnifying glass. You look for clues. You look for fingerprints. You look for footprints. You look for anything that will help you solve the mystery. The Old Testament is like a detective game. It is full of clues. It is full of fingerprints. It is full of footprints. And every clue points to one person. Every fingerprint belongs to one person. Every footprint belongs to one person. That person is Jesus.


This book is a 30 day adventure for you and your kids. We are going to be detectives. We are going to look for clues. We are going to follow the footprints. We are going to solve the mystery. You do not need to be a Bible expert to lead this. You just need to be willing to explore with your kids. Get ready to put on your detective hats. Get ready to grab your magnifying glasses. Get ready to find Jesus.


How to Use This Book


This is a 30 day journey. Each day takes about 5 to 10 minutes. Read the secret clue. Read the big reveal. Do the family activity together. Say the prayer out loud. Let your child color the picture. The goal is not perfection. The goal is connection. Have fun with it. Get messy. Ask questions. Laugh together. This is an adventure. Let us begin.

pages.body:
The Secret Clue (OT)
"Consecrate to me every firstborn male. The first offspring of every womb among the Israelites belongs to me, whether human or animal." - Exodus 13:2


The firstborn was special. The firstborn was set apart. The firstborn belonged to God. The firstborn was a clue. The firstborn was a fingerprint. The firstborn was a footprint. And the firstborn points to Jesus.


The Big Reveal (NT)
"For those God foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brothers and sisters." - Romans 8:29


Jesus is the firstborn. He is the firstborn of all creation. He is the firstborn from the dead. He is the firstborn among many brothers and sisters. The firstborn in the Old Testament is a clue. It is a fingerprint. It is a footprint. The reality is Jesus.


Family Activity
Make a list of the firstborns in your family. Talk about how the firstborn was special in the Old Testament. Talk about how Jesus is the firstborn. He is the special one. He is the one who saves us.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being the firstborn. Thank you for making me part of the family. Thank you for including me. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt
A family with a big heart in the middle.

"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: 'Select some towns to be your cities of refuge, to which a person who has killed someone accidentally may flee.'" - Numbers 35:10-11


The cities of refuge were clues. They were safe places. They were sanctuaries. The cities of refuge were fingerprints. They were footprints. And they point to Jesus.


The Big Reveal (NT)
"Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus." - Romans 8:1


Jesus is the city of refuge. He is the safe place. He is the sanctuary. He is the fulfillment of the cities of refuge. The cities of refuge in the Old Testament are clues. They are fingerprints. They are footprints. The reality is Jesus.


Family Activity
Find a quiet, safe place in your home. Sit there for a few minutes. Thank Jesus for being your city of refuge.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being my city of refuge. Thank you for being my safe place. Thank you for being my sanctuary. I love you. Amen."

The Secret Clue (OT)
"I establish my covenant with you: Never again will all life be destroyed by the waters of a flood; never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth." - Genesis 9:11


The covenant was a clue. The covenant was an agreement. It was a promise. The covenant was a fingerprint. The covenant was a footprint. And the covenant points to Jesus.


The Big Reveal (NT)
"In the same way, after the supper he took the cup, saying, 'This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.'" - Luke 22:20

A Note for the Parent: Building on the Foundation


You did it. You spent 30 days being detectives with your children. But the adventure does not end here. It is just beginning.


Here are a few tips to keep going:


1. Make it a habit, not a chore. Do not stress about reading the Bible for 30 minutes a day. A simple 5 minute rhythm before bed is better than an hour once a month.
2. Let them see you reading. Kids do what they see. Let them catch you reading your Bible. Let them see that it matters to you.
3. Ask "Where is Jesus?" in every story. Whenever you read a Bible story, ask your child, "Where do you see Jesus in this story?" This trains them to look for Jesus everywhere.
4. Recommended next steps. Read The Jesus Storybook Bible by Sally Lloyd-Jones. Read The Biggest Story by Kevin DeYoung. Keep pointing them to the Treasure.


You are doing a great job. Keep going.

If you loved this adventure, there is another one waiting for you. The Great Adventure takes you on a journey through connecting the lives of Old Testament heroes to Jesus. It is full of activities, coloring pages, and simple prayers.
